parsed.explanation: Visitor-facing record is strong: no criminalisation of trans expression, no documented border/document friction, transgender identity covered by hate-crime (2018) and hate-speech (2019) law with a functioning national dataset, depathologised since 2017, and a 2019 travel index ranking it among the most LGBT-friendly destinations. Recent legal reform (2024 acts, in force July 2025) and church same-sex marriage acceptance signal a generally trans-respecting institutional culture; rule of law works and society is broadly accepting. Deductions: an October 2025 national pool chain bars trans customers from choosing changing rooms — an everyday facility exposure reaching visitors, though commercial rather than state-imposed, contested in law, and of undocumented scope beyond that chain; hate-speech enforcement is limited by religious-speech rulings; and organised political opposition plus documented harassment of trans advocates raises the climate signal. Child clinical restrictions and LGR medical barriers are resident-facing and not scored.
